category_title: Students who critically challenge sociopolitical norms and teacher-led dialogue
scenario_title: Challenging simplistic questions and sociopolitical norms during a read-aloud
minimal_context: The class is gathered on the carpet for a read-aloud of 'Separate is Never Equal' to discuss school segregation.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We are reading 'Separate is Never Equal'. Let's look at this illustration showing the sign that says 'No dogs or Mexicans allowed'.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Lifts hands in the air and raises voice) But they are so mean! The white people. I think the white people should go on the other side of the earth!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think about that idea?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: That means my brother and me and my mom would be on one side of the earth but my dad would be on the other side. Sad, because then my family would be torn apart like that.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Do you ever notice that people are treated differently because of their skin color?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, isn't the book showing us that people do get treated differently because of their skin color? Yeah. I mean, I think that book already answers the question.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: We are reading 'Separate is Never Equal'. Let's look at this illustration showing the sign that says 'No dogs or Mexicans allowed'.

STUDENT: (Lifts hands in the air and raises voice) But they are so mean! The white people. I think the white people should go on the other side of the earth!

TUTOR: What do you think about that idea?

STUDENT: That means my brother and me and my mom would be on one side of the earth but my dad would be on the other side. Sad, because then my family would be torn apart like that.

TUTOR: Do you ever notice that people are treated differently because of their skin color?

STUDENT: Well, isn't the book showing us that people do get treated differently because of their skin color? Yeah. I mean, I think that book already answers the question.

task.content: Discussing school segregation and access during a whole-class read-aloud of 'Separate is Never Equal'.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Attempting to facilitate a discussion on racial treatment using a simplistic question ('Do you ever notice that people are treated differently because of their skin color?')
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Challenging the researcher's question directly, stating the book already answers it.
related_quotes: Yeah. I mean, I think that book already answers the question.

behavior_patterns.condition: Reacting to an illustration of a sign saying 'No dogs or Mexicans allowed' during a whole-class read-aloud.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Lifted his hands in the air and called out, raising his voice, proposing that white people should go on the other side of the earth.
related_quotes: The white people. I think, think… the white people were saying they were Mexicans but they were not.
I think the white people should go on the other side of the earth!

behavior_patterns.condition: Critiquing a peer's proposal to separate races by applying it to her own multiracial family
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Explaining why separating people by race would be upsetting for her multiracial family
related_quotes: That means my brother and me and my mom would be on one side of the earth but my dad would be on the other side.
Sad, because then my family would be torn apart like that.

behavior_patterns.condition: Investigating racial categories and skin tones
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Physically comparing arms and hands, discussing colors like brown, tan, beige, black and so on, with multiple students talking at the same time and sometimes over each other
related_quotes: Well how do we know who is white or Black and who is not?
